items.description: An incorrect authorization vulnerability in the SNMP parameter of Zyxel EE5301-00 customized firmware version 5.63(ACLD.2)b3_D0 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition on an affected device.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the multisite Redis configuration store that is not tenant-scoped. As a result, tenant administrators can read and overwrite the master instance's effective configuration. Attackers can save configuration through /admin/api/configuration, optionally resetting storage.redisPrefix, to redirect master SMTP, set a known API token, or alter authentication settings.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject javascript: links via FAQ comments. When the comment editor is enabled, Utils::parseUrl() strips https:// from sanitized hrefs, turning an allowed https://javascript:443/ link into executable script that runs on the shared admin origin when clicked.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass that lets category- or language-restricted editors rewrite visibility ACLs and tags of any FAQ. Attackers send faq/update requests with a target faqId and an untranslated lang to expose restricted FAQs, wipe tags, or overwrite orphaned FAQs.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.0 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that exposes restricted and inactive category metadata to unauthenticated visitors. Attackers can enumerate category IDs via /category/{id}/{slug}.html or query /api/v4.0/categories to read names, descriptions, images and FAQ counts of restricted categories.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read editor-only Private Notes by querying the public FAQ list API. Attackers can page through GET /api/v4.0/faqs or /api/v3.1/faqs without credentials to retrieve the notes field of every anonymously readable FAQ, exposing internal remarks and ticket details.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in its public FAQ REST API that exposes author names and e-mail addresses to unauthenticated callers. Attackers can query the faq and paginated faqs endpoints to bulk-harvest e-mails and de-anonymise users who opted out of GDPR author visibility.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.0 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in POST /api/webauthn/prepare that creates accounts as active, bypassing manual activation and domain whitelisting. Anonymous attackers can obtain the freely issued CSRF token and register an activated account with an unverified email to access registered-user-only content and functions.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authentication bypass in password reset, letting external-identity accounts receive local passwords. Attackers with mailbox access can request reset tokens for OIDC, Keycloak, Entra ID, LDAP, SSO, or WebAuthn accounts and log in locally, skipping IdP MFA and deprovisioning.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored sql injection vulnerability in the MySQL driver that allows database users with table creation rights to inject SQL through unescaped geometry column names in unconvert_field(). Attackers can craft a column name containing an SQL expression that executes with another AdminNeo user's privileges when they edit a row, save it, or export the table.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read unpublished FAQ titles via bookmark_action. Attackers can request FAQ detail pages with bookmark_action=add across sequential ids, then view /user/bookmarks to reveal draft and pending submission question text.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows category- or language-restricted editors to bypass scoped rights via public REST write endpoints. Attackers with a scoped right and the shared API token can use PUT faq/update, POST faq/create, and POST category to rewrite published FAQs and create root categories outside their scope.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in POST /admin/api/faq/import that lets FAQ_ADD users bypass the FAQ_PUBLISH right. Authenticated contributors can upload a CSV with column 8 set to true to publish unreviewed, optionally sticky FAQs such as phishing content.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an improper reference counting flaw on multisite deployments, allowing editors to delete other instances' attachment files. Because linkedRecords() counts only the local faqattachment table, deleting an attachment with shared md5 content makes File::delete() unlink the shared blob, destroying another instance's files.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows delegated group or user admins to remove rights they do not hold by submitting empty rights lists. Attackers can send an empty rightIds or userRights array to group/permissions or user/update-rights to wipe all rights of more-privileged groups or administrators.

phpMyFAQ 3.2.5 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the user/request-removal API endpoint that lets authenticated users file account removal requests as other users. The ownership check calls getUserById() with the attacker-supplied userId on the session user object, so it compares the input against the target's own record. Attackers who know a victim's login name and email can submit that userId, loginname, and email, sending administrators a spoofed Remove User Request email. This may lead an admin to delete the victim's account and data.

phpMyFAQ 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated frontend users to receive restricted FAQ titles by subscribing to Web Push notifications. When editors publish user/group-restricted FAQs, WebPushService::sendToAll() delivers the question, FAQ id, category, and slugified URL to every subscriber, bypassing the FAQ ACL.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an sql injection vulnerability in the ClickHouse driver because idf_escape() doubles backticks but does not escape backslashes in identifiers. Attackers can lure a logged-in user into opening a GET link with a column name ending in a backslash in columns, where, or order parameters, causing query text to be parsed as SQL.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows database users to inject markup into another user's session via column type names rendered with innerHTML. Attackers can create a PostgreSQL type or table with markup in its name to render live elements in the help popup, enabling content spoofing and requests to attacker servers.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Admin::printTablePartitions() that allows authenticated users to inject HTML by placing markup in partition column names. Attackers with CREATE or ALTER privileges can create a partitioned table whose unescaped partition expression executes script when another user opens the table-structure page.
